I've been playing over the past several days, and I've contrived several neat stratagems.

1) If you're a larger blob (around top 10), hunt for prey exclusively in one quadrant. Once you happen to encounter fish that are closer to the corner than you, begin running them down with the intent to crush them against the walls. If executed properly, you can get at least some of their mass (eat half of them as they split to run).

2) If you're middlingly large, you can hunt for prey near one of the larger players. Same strategy as corner-hunting, only you have to be careful not to be subsumed by the larger blob.

3) If you're split into 16 blobs, you can eat the green spikes with impunity. You'll be at your max-cell number, so you can just consume the mass that's contained within. A nice way of turning the tide while all the little ones begin to pick at your flesh.

BASIC SURVIVAL TIP #1: Always, always be fearful of the prospective single-cell blob that has the mass to split and kill you. They WILL do so without warning, and it occurs rapidly enough that you will be dead before you can react.

BASIC SURVIVAL TIP #2: If you're being chased, take cover next to one of their rivals and stay out of the vector at which they'll split. Doing so allows you to deincentivize your capture: in going for you, they'll be exposing themselves to aforementioned rivals.
